open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
open_points.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding”
open_points.question: Which exact fields count as client-supplied Registry context, and is the required project_id on snapshot and other project-scoped requests explicitly exempt from “project facts”?
options: Reject only Registry-derived fields such as status, display name, address and customer_ref while accepting project_id
Treat project_id as a forbidden project fact, which would reject otherwise required project-scoped requests
open_points.default_guess: Accept project_id and reject only client-supplied Registry-derived context.

witness.initial: An active producer has permission to import a snapshot for an active Registry project.
events: The producer submits a valid SnapshotPublication containing its required project_id and no status, display name, address or customer_ref.
outcomes: The decoder accepts project_id as an identity selector and proceeds to the Registry-backed guard.
The decoder treats project_id as a client-supplied project fact and refuses the request before the Registry call.
witness.observer: The producer sees either an import result or a decoding refusal.

open_points.subject: INV-001, INV-017 and PLAT-REG-003 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-001, INV-017, PLAT-REG-003 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check establishes the untested parts of these invariants: complete first-failure ordering, uniqueness of active staff assignments, and refusal when Registry validation returns a UUID different from the requested UUID?
options: Extend the bound check to assert every claimed part
Bind additional checks that assert the missing cases
Narrow the claimed invariants or binding to what the check actually establishes
open_points.default_guess: Extend or supplement the check so every named invariant is fully asserted.

open_points.subject: INV-004 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-004 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves that every authentication failure is externally indistinguishable with respect to account existence and cannot expose project data?
options: Extend the bound check across all authentication-failure classes and visible outputs
Bind another comprehensive concealment check
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add comprehensive comparisons of status, body, headers, audit-visible behavior and project-data absence.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves that no Registry snapshot is stored or reused as current truth, that context is fetched live, and that archived context remains readable while granting no mutation permission?
options: Strengthen the existing checks collectively to cover every clause
Add a dedicated persistence-and-freshness check
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add a dedicated check that changes Registry answers between calls and inspects persistence for cached current context.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-001 Registry linkage binding
open_points.text: “no service code generates a project id, the gateway only reads, and every project id the portal stores is one the Registry issued”
open_points.question: What check establishes this universally rather than only scanning selected UUID constructors and excluding seeded project IDs from the stored-ID assertion?
options: Use exhaustive construction/storage instrumentation that attributes every stored project_id to a Registry-issued value
Expand static and runtime checks to cover all generation paths and seeded rows
Narrow the claim to the paths actually checked
open_points.default_guess: Instrument all project_id writes and require Registry provenance for every value.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-005 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:api_transport_financial_policy_registry_gateway_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check exercises every closed RegistryFailureKind translation and proves that none falls back to cached, client-supplied or fabricated context?
options: Extend the existing checks to cover the complete table and every prohibited fallback
Add a table-driven gateway check
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add a table-driven check covering every condition, precedence and fallback prohibition.

open_points.subject: INV-031 expense-recognition witness
open_points.text: “an unconfirmed, incomplete, unsupported-version or provider-carrying result is refused at decoding, by create_expense_from_recognition and over HTTP, with every table unchanged”
open_points.question: What check exercises every named invalid form at each of the three claimed boundaries?
options: Add the missing boundary/form combinations to the bound check
Split the claim among separate decoder, use-case and HTTP checks
Narrow the claim to the combinations actually tested
open_points.default_guess: Use a matrix covering every invalid form at decoding, direct use-case invocation and HTTP.

open_points.subject: INV-009 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal].” and “INV-009 [witness: verification:viewer_access_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Does each check bind only the grant-uniqueness clause it tests, or must each independently assert both viewer-grant and service-principal-grant uniqueness?
options: Split INV-009 or qualify each binding by its tested clause
Make each bound check assert both uniqueness clauses
Bind a combined check that asserts the whole invariant
open_points.default_guess: Bind one combined check, or split the invariant into separately identified clauses.

open_points.subject: INV-042 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-042 [witness: verification:project_tracking_audit_writer_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves, in addition to payment-id replay, that WorkPayment never creates a factura or accounting posting and that payments_total is derived?
options: Extend the bound check to inspect forbidden postings and recompute the total
Bind additional checks for the non-accounting and derivation clauses
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit absence-of-posting and read-time-total assertions.

open_points.subject: INV-043 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-043 [witness: verification:photo_management_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves that every visibility-only photo change preserves all financial and progress data?
options: Compare all financial and progress tables and derived views before and after visibility changes
Bind a dedicated non-interference check
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Compare every relevant table and derived view before and after the change.

open_points.subject: INV-037 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-037 [witness: verification:project_tracking_audit_writer_sqlite_uow_client_portal].” and “INV-037 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check establishes EUR-only handling, explicit foreign-currency refusal without conversion, two-fraction-digit semantics and ROUND_HALF_UP for every monetary boundary covered by INV-037?
options: Extend the existing checks into a complete boundary matrix
Add a rules-table property check covering every money-bearing operation
Narrow the invariant or bindings
open_points.default_guess: Add a table-driven property check for all money-bearing boundaries.

open_points.subject: INV-041 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-041 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check asserts the exact weighted-progress formula, per-section rounded completed values, and unavailable progress when the denominator is zero?
options: Extend the bound check with exact expected values and zero-denominator cases
Bind a dedicated financial-policy property check
Narrow the binding or invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add exact multi-section calculations and zero-denominator cases.

open_points.subject: INV-044 witness binding
open_points.text: “a section without a progress record reads completion None and completed work value None”
open_points.question: What check actually asserts completed_work_value is None, rather than merely recording the observed value while allowing 0.00?
options: Add a direct None assertion in both budget and progress views
Bind a regenerated implementation check after the required Route B change
Narrow the claimed witness until the implementation changes
open_points.default_guess: Regenerate the views and assert None directly at both projection boundaries.

open_points.subject: INV-015 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-015 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What exact enhanced audit facts constitute INV-015, and what check asserts them beyond administrator authorization and the presence of one recovery-override audit?
options: Define and test the required actor provenance and exceptional-flow metadata
Narrow “enhanced audit” to the fields currently asserted
Bind a separate audit-detail check
open_points.default_guess: Define the enhanced fields explicitly and assert their exact values.

open_points.subject: INV-005 and INV-006 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-005, INV-006 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal].” and the two separate INV-006 bindings
open_points.question: What check covers revoked credentials and directly proves that disabled staff and disabled service principals retain no usable credential or session across every affected contour?
options: Extend the three checks collectively to cover every cascade row
Add a table-driven revocation-cascade check
Narrow individual bindings to the rows they assert
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven check for every revoked or disabled object and every affected authentication mechanism.

open_points.subject: INV-029 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-029 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal]; INV-029 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check performs an actual producer import with invalid content and proves scope authorization runs before content validation?
options: Add an import-level ordering scenario to one bound check
Bind a dedicated producer-import ordering check
Narrow the binding to scope decisions only
open_points.default_guess: Add an import request that fails both scope and content and assert the scope refusal with no import record.

open_points.subject: INV-051 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-051 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves exactly one AuditRecord with correct actor provenance for every catalog action, including service actors and key_version?
options: Add a catalog-driven audit check
Extend the existing check to all actions and actor kinds
Narrow the invariant or binding
open_points.default_guess: Add a catalog-driven check covering every action and actor provenance shape.

open_points.subject: INV-053 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-053 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check asserts result=rejected as well as a closed reason_code for every rejected significant-mutation audit row it exercises?
options: Assert both fields on every generated rejected row
Bind a generic append_audit validation check
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Assert result and reason_code together for each rejection case.

open_points.subject: INV-018 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-018 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check covers Unicode casefolding, all whitespace refusal and the accepted email syntax validation?
options: Extend the check with Unicode, internal/surrounding whitespace and invalid-syntax cases
Bind a dedicated normalization property check
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add table-driven normalization and refusal cases.

open_points.subject: INV-019 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-019 [witness: verification:credential_security_policy_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check asserts rejection below 12 and above 128 Unicode code points and rejection of every accepted control-character class?
options: Extend the bound check with boundary and control-set cases
Bind a dedicated password-policy check
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add exact length-boundary and control-character tests.

open_points.subject: INV-020 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-020 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check attempts and refuses mutation and deletion of an already accepted snapshot, rather than testing only duplicate insertion?
options: Add repository update and delete attempts
Bind an append-only persistence check
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit update and deletion attempts and assert unchanged storage.

open_points.subject: INV-022 through INV-025 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-022, INV-023, INV-024, INV-025 [witness: verification:budget_management_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves producer activation is impossible, imported plans are immutable, activation is atomic under injected failure, and automatic linking uses source_key only with no display-name match?
options: Extend the bound check to every missing clause
Split the invariants among dedicated checks
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add dedicated capability, immutability, failure-injection and linking cases.

open_points.subject: INV-026 conflict behavior
open_points.text: A18 requires “a changed re-publication is a conflict that changes nothing”, while R0-25 and M19 require a classified integrity conflict to create “a fresh immutable import result with a fresh import_id and its snapshot.import audit”.
open_points.question: Does a changed re-publication leave every table unchanged, or does it append the required conflict import record and audit while leaving snapshot, budget and expense state unchanged?
options: No table changes at all
Append the conflict import record and audit, but change no snapshot, budget, plan or expense rows
open_points.default_guess: Append the conflict import record and audit; interpret the no-change rule as applying only to business and snapshot state.

witness.initial: A snapshot for project P, estimate E, version 1 has been accepted.
events: The same producer republishes E version 1 with changed content after passing access checks.
outcomes: A18's required test permits no table to change.
R0-25 and M19 append a new SnapshotImportRecord with outcome integrity_conflict and one snapshot.import audit record.
witness.observer: The producer sees either no import result or a fresh conflict import_id; administrators also see different audit history.

open_points.subject: INV-026, INV-027 and INV-028 witness binding
open_points.text: “INV-026, INV-027, INV-028: the budget derivation check”
open_points.question: What non-heuristic check proves absence of every derived-value column and every section-removal surface, and how does the check reconcile its allowed conflict import/audit writes with the claimed unchanged state?
options: Replace heuristic scans with schema/interface enumeration and precise table-specific assertions
Add separate authoritative checks for each invariant
Narrow the witness claims
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit schema and store-surface inventories and limit unchanged-state assertions to the tables the invariant actually protects.

open_points.subject: INV-032 and INV-036 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-032, INV-036 [witness: verification:expense_intake_uow_client_portal].” and “INV-032, INV-036 [witness: verification:expense_management_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check injects failure between amount correction and allocation replacement and proves rollback preserves the sum invariant at every commit point?
options: Add failure injection between the two writes
Enforce and test the invariant at transaction commit independently of operation sequencing
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add commit-time validation plus a failure-injection rollback test.

open_points.subject: INV-035 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-035 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check proves unconfirmed expenses never enter totals, in addition to testing excluded expenses?
options: Seed an unconfirmed expense through a lower-level violating fixture and assert exclusion
Bind an intake check proving unconfirmed expenses cannot exist
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Use a violating persistence fixture and assert derived totals ignore it.

open_points.subject: INV-052 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-052 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check attempts and refuses updates and deletions of both audit records and import records?
options: Add update/delete attempts for both record types
Bind a generic append-only repository check
Narrow the binding
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit mutation and deletion attempts against both stores.

open_points.subject: TXN-002 witness binding
open_points.text: “TXN-001, TXN-002: the transaction guard check [witness: verification:transaction_guard_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check establishes that the exact original domain-error object, including its contents, is re-raised unchanged rather than merely an exception of the same type?
options: Assert object identity and payload equality
Narrow “unchanged” to same exception type
Bind an additional identity-preservation check
open_points.default_guess: Assert that the caught object is the same exception instance raised inside the transaction.

open_points.subject: TRN-001 through TRN-003 witness bindings
open_points.text: “TRN-001, TRN-002, TRN-003: the runtime behaviour check”; “TRN-001, TRN-003: the transport guard check”; “TRN-002: the API transport check”
open_points.question: What checks prove handler non-entry for every rejected host/body request, foreign-origin sign-out refusal, and absence of every actual credential, cookie or secret value from emitted logs?
options: Extend the existing checks with handler sentinels, cross-origin sign-out and injected real secrets
Add dedicated checks for each transport invariant
Narrow the bindings
open_points.default_guess: Add handler-entry sentinels, a foreign-origin sign-out case, and capture actual emitted logs containing representative secret values.

open_points.subject: wall-clock reading cardinality
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and “the wall clock gives the instant … one reading per request”, while “the audit writer takes [occurred_at] when it appends”.
open_points.question: Is the wall clock read once per HTTP request, once per operation, or once by each operation plus an additional audit-writer read?
options: One wall instant is captured per request and shared by all operations and audit appends
Each operation captures one wall instant, while the audit writer may capture another
Each operation and the audit writer independently read the clock once
open_points.default_guess: Each use-case operation reads once, and the audit writer obtains its exceptional occurred_at through a separate clock-source read.

witness.initial: A single HTTP mutation invokes one use case that writes created_at and appends an AuditRecord.
events: The use case needs its operation instant.
The audit writer appends and needs occurred_at.
outcomes: The request performs one wall-clock read and both timestamps use it.
The operation reads once and the audit writer performs a second read, so occurred_at may differ.
witness.observer: A reader of the business record and its audit record sees equal or differing timestamps, and clock instrumentation sees one or two reads.

open_points.subject: source-supplied timestamp representation
open_points.text: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes” but source times “are kept as supplied”, while State 1 originally types timestamps as timezone-aware UTC and says A28 narrows persisted storage to offset-naive.
open_points.question: When a source supplies an offset-aware UTC datetime, is the stored field converted to offset-naive UTC or persisted in its supplied aware representation?
options: Preserve the instant but normalize storage to offset-naive UTC
Preserve the source value and its timezone-aware representation exactly
open_points.default_guess: Normalize to offset-naive UTC while preserving the represented instant.

witness.initial: A producer has a valid snapshot whose approved_at is 2026-11-08T12:00:00+00:00.
events: The portal accepts and persists ApprovedEstimateSnapshot.approved_at.
outcomes: The database stores 2026-11-08 12:00:00 without tzinfo under the universal persisted-timestamp rule.
The database stores the timezone-aware +00:00 value because source-supplied times are kept as supplied.
witness.observer: Repository readers and serialized snapshot details observe different datetime representations.

open_points.subject: clock invariant witness coverage
open_points.text: “A test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades, bootstrap) that its written timestamps, other than audit occurred_at, are one instant.”
open_points.question: What bound checks cover activation, every revocation cascade, expiry=instant+TTL and preservation of every source-supplied time, rather than only selected service-identity operations and bootstrap?
options: Add one bound check for every named multi-write operation and invariant clause
Bind a generic injected-clock property suite across all operations
Narrow the invariant or test claim
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected-clock suite enumerating every timestamp-writing operation.

open_points.subject: configuration invariant witness bindings
open_points.text: “The existence of every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound is invariant; its value is configuration.”
open_points.question: What check enumerates every required timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound and proves each exists and is configuration-driven?
options: Create an authoritative configuration inventory and test every entry
Extend the two checks to cover all settings
Narrow the invariant to the settings currently verified
open_points.default_guess: Add an authoritative inventory with missing, malformed and overridden-value cases for every setting.

open_points.subject: security-review invariant binding
open_points.text: “Every category resolves to an accepted decision or an open question.”
open_points.question: How does the check prove that NOT_APPLICABLE categories also resolve as required, rather than accepting a rationale without either an accepted decision or an open question?
options: Require every category, including NOT_APPLICABLE, to reference a decision or open question
Change the invariant to allow a justified NOT_APPLICABLE outcome
Add a separate accepted disposition type for NOT_APPLICABLE
open_points.default_guess: Change the invariant to explicitly recognize a justified NOT_APPLICABLE disposition, then test it.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 coverage of transitive distributions
open_points.text: The normative rule checks “the pinned versions”, while the Required test says “the deploy step judges every distribution installed in the built image” and refuses any “listed version”.
open_points.question: Does a known vulnerability in an installed transitive distribution block deployment even though transitive libraries are not pinned and DEP-002 is phrased only in terms of pins?
options: Every vulnerable installed distribution blocks deployment
Only directly pinned distributions block deployment
open_points.default_guess: Every vulnerable installed distribution blocks deployment, matching the release-gate test.

witness.initial: All four direct pins have no listed vulnerability, but pip resolves a transitive distribution whose installed version has a listed vulnerability.
events: The pre-deploy vulnerability gate evaluates it.
outcomes: Deployment proceeds because no deployed pin is vulnerable under the normative rule and formal invariant.
Deployment is refused because the Required test judges every installed distribution.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees the service start or remain stopped.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 advisory freshness
open_points.text: “against a fresh public advisory snapshot” and “only on a recent passing verdict”; “stale … data … does not start it”
open_points.question: What exact age or validity rule separates fresh/recent evidence from stale evidence?
options: A fixed maximum age measured from advisory snapshot and verdict timestamps
Freshness delegated to the advisory provider's validity metadata
No time threshold, only a requirement to fetch during the deploy
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit configured maximum age checked against the deployment clock.

witness.initial: An image has a passing vulnerability verdict bound to its exact content id, produced from advisory data one hour ago.
events: A deployment starts without obtaining newer advisory data.
outcomes: The one-hour-old verdict is recent and the service starts.
The verdict is stale and deployment is refused.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees whether the release starts.
